question: When you click a layer in the Layers list and its settings need room above, when should the list make way?
context: With nothing picked, the Layers and Library pane now fills the panel (2026-10-18). Picking a layer from that list brings its settings in above, so the pane has to shrink.

options.label: Wait until the pointer leaves the list
options.summary: The row you clicked stays exactly under the pointer. The picked layer's settings slide in above as soon as you move the pointer out of the list, toward them.
pros: A second click on the same spot never misses, which you asked for on 2026-10-14
Moving toward the settings is what reveals them, so they appear where you are heading
cons: Right after the click the settings are not visible yet, so it can look as if the click did nothing
options.mitigation: The row lights up as picked at once, and on the canvas the layer gets its handles straight away.

options.label: Make way at once; the list slides down
options.summary: The settings appear above the moment you click, and the Layers list slides down by however much room they take, carrying the row you clicked away from the pointer.
pros: The settings are on screen in the same frame as the click
cons: The row you clicked moves out from under the pointer, often by a few hundred points, so a quick second click lands on a different row
options.mitigation: The list keeps the picked row on screen after it slides.

options.label: Wait a beat, then make way
options.summary: The list holds still for about half a second after a click in it, then slides down and the settings appear, whether or not the pointer has moved.
pros: Quick double clicks still land where you aimed
The settings appear without having to move the pointer
cons: The list moves under a pointer that is sitting still, which can surprise you mid-read
options.mitigation: The slide uses the same short curve as a section folding, so it reads as one motion.
